## My thinking, as this farmer

I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life — I'm 63, my back isn't what it was, and my three children all work in Shijiazhuang and Handan now. It's just me and my wife working the 10 mu of contracted land.

I don't change what works. Everyone here grows **winter wheat then summer corn** on the same land — that's the rotation my father did, and his father before him. The soil here on the North China Plain is suited to it, and I know exactly what it needs.

My wheat is already in the ground — planted last October. Right now it's jointing up. I'll apply urea soon as a topdress, then irrigate if it stays dry. I used 济麦22 seed — that's what the supply station sells, it yields well here, disease isn't too bad. I put down compound fertilizer (复合肥) at planting. I'll spray herbicide in spring and watch for rust — if neighbors are seeing it, I'll spray a fungicide too.

After I harvest wheat in June, I clear the stubble fast and plant corn straight away — no ploughing, the machines just punch seed into the ground now. I'll buy 郑单958 hybrid from the township shop — that's been my corn seed for fifteen years. Reliable. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress urea when the corn is knee high. I'll water once in August if the rain doesn't come.

I don't experiment with new varieties or special techniques. I'm 63. I just want a stable harvest, sell the grain to the state purchaser, and have enough to live on.
